critical_issues.msg: ticket.customer_id is read on line 86 but const ticket is assigned on line 94 — temporal dead zone violation; will crash at runtime if the variable naming order is ever changed or if a linter reorders declarations.
critical_issues.suggestion: Move `const ticket = ticketData?.data as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;` (line 94) above the `customerName` const (line 86).

critical_issues.msg: ApiEnvelope<T>.data is typed as PaginatedResponse<T>, which is wrong for non-paginated endpoints (slaBreaches, useReminders, useActivities single-item, etc.) — callers accessing .data.items will fail at runtime for those hooks.
critical_issues.suggestion: Split ApiEnvelope into ApiEnvelope<T> with optional fields or a looser data type, or make data: T directly and adjust callers.

critical_issues.msg: useReminders calls apiClient.get without a type argument, and ApiEnvelope<PaginatedResponse<unknown>> is incorrectly applied to a non-paginated endpoint, so the return type is wrong.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add the correct type argument to apiClient.get<...> and update ApiEnvelope usage for the reminders endpoint.

critical_issues.msg: bulk_update_tickets iterates over body.ticket_ids sequentially and calls update_ticket N times — N+1 query pattern (Rule 85). A single tenant with 500 tickets triggers 500 individual UPDATE calls.
critical_issues.suggestion: Batch the update into one or two SQL statements: use `await session.execute(update(TicketModel).where(and_(TicketModel.id.in_(body.ticket_ids), TicketModel.tenant_id == ctx.tenant_id)).values(...))` for the common fields, then refresh the affected rows in a single query.

critical_issues.msg: bulk_update_tickets has no transaction scope across the loop — if the loop partially completes and an exception fires, some tickets are updated and some are not with no rollback.
critical_issues.suggestion: Wrap the entire loop (or the batched query) in a try block, or restructure as a single batch UPDATE so all-or-nothing semantics are guaranteed by the router's commit lifecycle.

suggestions.msg: Implementation plan document; no review issues.
useCustomers(1, 100) fetches up to 100 customer records just to look up one name by ID — wasteful O(N) operation; a dedicated useCustomer(ticket.customer_id) query should be used instead.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace useCustomers(1, 100) with a useCustomer(ticket?.customer_id) hook from queries.ts.

suggestions.msg: updateTicket is assigned but never used — dead code.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the `const updateTicket = useUpdateTicket();` declaration on line 81 and the corresponding useUpdateTicket import on line 8.

suggestions.msg: TicketFormDialog receives initialData without assigned_to, priority, and sla_level — editing will lose these fields since the dialog pre-fills from initialData.
suggestions.suggestion: Add assigned_to: ticket.assigned_to as number, priority: ticket.priority as string, sla_level: ticket.sla_level as string to the initialData prop.

suggestions.msg: handleDelete only sets deleteDialogOpen to true without performing any action; the actual delete call is in an inline async arrow function inside the Dialog's onClick, mixing UI state management with business logic.
suggestions.suggestion: Move the async delete call into handleDelete so the handler owns the complete action, not the JSX.

suggestions.msg: initials() will return an empty string for names that are empty or contain only whitespace characters (split segments will be empty strings that are filtered to nothing by [0] access on empty strings).
suggestions.suggestion: Add a guard: if (!name?.trim()) return '?'; before the split.

suggestions.msg: useEffect dependency array includes ticket and ticketId but not ticket.response_deadline — not strictly incorrect due to the ref guard, but incomplete for exhaustive-deps correctness.
suggestions.suggestion: Add ticket.response_deadline to the dependency array, or restructure so the condition is checked inside the effect body.

suggestions.msg: useEffect cleanup returns a function that clears timerRef but timerRef is also set to null inside clearSearch — redundant but harmless.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the useEffect entirely; the debounce timer is already cleared inside clearSearch and handleChange.

suggestions.msg: handleDeleteTicket shows a window.confirm dialog instead of a styled UI dialog; this pattern inconsistently mixes browser-native UX with the design system.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace window.confirm with a dedicated confirmation dialog component, consistent with the edit/delete dialog pattern used elsewhere.

suggestions.msg: handleViewTicket fires the SLA breach toast only when navigating to a ticket, even though breachedTicketIds is already shown in a batch toast on mount — redundant for the same user session.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the toast from handleViewTicket since breached toasts already fire on page load, or scope it only to non-breached tickets visited from outside the list.

suggestions.msg: useUsers is called inside the component body and then usersData is conditionally read inside an if block — this is technically fine because useUsers always runs, but it is fragile: adding any statement before the if that depends on usersData would break the rules-of-hooks ordering.
suggestions.suggestion: Move users extraction before the if block: `const users = (usersData?.data?.items ?? []) as ...; if (selectedIds.size === 0) return null;` — same pattern used in page.tsx.

suggestions.msg: useEffect dependency array includes createdAt and slaLevel but neither is referenced inside the effect — changes to these props will not restart the interval, making the dependency list misleading.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove createdAt and slaLevel from the useEffect dependency array, or remove the empty deps comment if intentionally static.

suggestions.msg: useEffect dependency array declares createdAt and slaLevel but neither is referenced in the effect body — the timer will not restart when these values change, making the deps misleading.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove createdAt and slaLevel from the dependency array, or add a comment explaining why they are absent.

suggestions.msg: When breached is true, className is replaced with `${colorClass} animate-pulse border-red-500` and the incoming className prop is discarded — this silently drops the caller's className on breached tickets.
suggestions.suggestion: Merge className into the breached branch: `breached ? \`${colorClass} animate-pulse border-red-500 ${className ?? ""}\` : colorClass + (className ? \` \${className\}` : "")`

suggestions.msg: cn is imported from @/lib/utils but never used.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the unused import.

suggestions.msg: useCustomers is called with page=1, pageSize=20 to populate a dropdown selector, but only one customer is ever displayed at a time; no pagination controls exist for the dropdown, so a customer not on page 1 is unreachable.
suggestions.suggestion: Use useSearchCustomers with debouncing for the dropdown, or increase pageSize to a large value and rely on the Select UI for filtering.

suggestions.msg: The channel, priority, and sla_level selects are hidden in edit mode, but their form values are never cleared; if the user toggles from edit back to create, stale values from the last create session may persist.
suggestions.suggestion: Reset channel, priority, and sla_level in the useEffect that resets the form when initialData changes.

suggestions.msg: customer_id is not registered with react-hook-form — only a hidden input with a validator is used — so programmatic form inspection (e.g. formValues in onSubmit) may behave unexpectedly.
suggestions.suggestion: Register customer_id with register() and manage it via a controlled Select with onChange updating a hidden field, or use Controller.

suggestions.msg: Comments section header for Tasks is missing a leading // comment prefix and will be parsed as live code by some linters.
has_next is declared in PaginatedResponse but no hook uses it — pagination in callers relies on total and page_size for manual next/prev logic.
suggestions.suggestion: No fix needed; has_next is available for future use if callers add next-page buttons.

suggestions.msg: mypy is listed in dev dependencies but no [tool.mypy] configuration exists in the file.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a [tool.mypy] table with at least ignores = ["attr-defined"] and strict = true (or a project-chosen baseline), and configure mypy.ini or pyproject.toml overrides so `mypy src/` runs with consistent settings across machines.

suggestions.msg: Ruff formatter configuration is absent — only [tool.ruff.lint] is specified, so `ruff format` has no project-level settings (e.g. indent width, quote style) and will fall back to defaults.
suggestions.suggestion: Add [tool.ruff.format] with options matching the project's style (e.g. indent-width = 4, quote-style = "double") so formatting is deterministic and reproducible.

suggestions.msg: HTTPException is imported but never raised in this file — all error paths delegate to the global AppException handler.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the HTTPException import. If a future endpoint needs it, add it back then.

suggestions.msg: assigned_to: ge=0 accepts 0 as valid, but the create_ticket handler treats 0 as a sentinel for 'unassigned', creating an inconsistency: a client can send assigned_to=0 but it will be silently interpreted as unassigned.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the ge=0 constraint and let the TicketCreate schema omit assigned_to entirely when unassigned, matching the existing comment in list_tickets that documents 0 as 'unassigned'.

suggestions.msg: Docstring says 'Tickets that do not exist or belong to a different tenant are skipped' but update_ticket raises NotFoundException for missing tickets, causing the loop to abort on the first missing ID rather than skip.
suggestions.suggestion: Catch NotFoundException inside the loop, log the skipped ID, and continue — matching the documented contract.

suggestions.msg: check_sla_status endpoint creates two separate TicketService(session) instances (one for get_ticket, one inside SLAService constructor), and SLAService constructs a third TicketService at line 408.
suggestions.suggestion: Reuse a single TicketService instance across the endpoint's logic: pass ticket_svc = TicketService(session) into SLAService(session, ticket_service=ticket_svc) and remove the redundant construction at line 408.

suggestions.msg: ticket_service parameter has no type annotation and defaults to None — violates Rule 121/CLAUDE.md: 'Every service __init__ that takes a session must type it as AsyncSession with no default' and the same discipline should apply to injected dependencies.
suggestions.suggestion: Type the parameter as `ticket_service: TicketService | None = None` to make the optional contract explicit and catch type errors at static-analysis time.

suggestions.msg: get_breach_tickets signature mixes two responsibilities — if tickets is provided it is filtered; if not, it is fetched from the injected ticket_service. The conditional at line 44 makes it unclear whether callers passing tickets intend to bypass the service query or are accidentally shadowing it.
suggestions.suggestion: Split into two methods: get_breach_tickets_from_list(tickets: list[Ticket]) for filtering a pre-fetched list, and get_breach_tickets(tenant_id: int) that always fetches via ticket_service. Remove the conditional.

suggestions.msg: remaining.total_seconds() is called twice — once in the comparison and once to produce the warning threshold.
suggestions.suggestion: Compute it once: remaining_secs = remaining.total_seconds(); then use remaining_secs < warning_threshold * 3600 and remaining_secs for the hours calculation.

suggestions.msg: The function-level type hint Literal["normal", "warning", "breached"] is returned at line 16 but get_breach_tickets at line 42 returns TicketModel objects (or list[Ticket]) — a docstring/return-type mismatch.
suggestions.suggestion: Ensure docstrings document actual return types accurately.

suggestions.msg: _AGENT_POOL is a module-level constant (1, 2, 3) with no way to configure it per tenant or via environment — if the agent pool changes, the service must be edited and deployed.
suggestions.suggestion: Load from an environment variable or a config object: _AGENT_POOL = tuple(int(x) for x in os.environ.get("AGENT_POOL_IDS", "1,2,3").split(",")) so operators can change it without a code change.

suggestions.msg: assigned_to.is_not(None) correctly filters non-null assignees but the intent comment in tickets.py line 154 treats 0 as 'unassigned' — if assigned_to=0 is ever stored, it would be counted as assigned here.
suggestions.suggestion: Clarify whether 0 is ever a valid assigned_to value in the database, and add a comment explaining the null-vs-0 distinction if they have different meanings.

suggestions.msg: scalar() is used without checking whether the count query returned None — the fallback `or 0` is correct but the pattern is inconsistent with line 347 where the same fallback appears.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a comment or extract to a helper `_safe_count(result) -> int` to make the fallback intent explicit and reduce copy-paste risk.

suggestions.msg: get_sla_breaches performs a full table scan filtering by tenant_id and resolved_at IS NULL — if the tickets table grows large, there is no index to support this query efficiently.
suggestions.suggestion: Verify an index exists on (tenant_id, resolved_at, response_deadline) or create one. Check via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on a realistic dataset.

suggestions.msg: get_customer_tickets uses a LIKE pattern on ActivityModel.content (line 455) with string interpolation — while SQLAlchemy's .like() prevents injection, pattern-matching on a free-text content column prevents index usage.
suggestions.suggestion: If activity records are tied to a ticket via a ticket_id FK column, use that for the join instead of LIKE '%ticket#<id>%' to allow an index scan. If the current design is intentional, document the performance implication.

suggestions.msg: get_ticket_activity silently returns an empty list when no matching activities are found — this is a valid state but the docstring does not clarify that an empty list is the expected return value rather than an error.
suggestions.suggestion: Add 'Returns an empty list if no activity records exist.' to the docstring for clarity.

suggestions.msg: Test 'test_assign_ticket' asserts `assigned_to is not None` on a freshly created ticket, but tickets are auto-assigned on creation (ticket_service.py:120-121). The assertion only confirms the pre-existing auto-assignment, not that assign_ticket can reassign an already-assigned ticket.
suggestions.suggestion: Split into two tests: (1) test that creation auto-assigns (assert assigned_to is not None), (2) test that assign_ticket can override an existing assignment by assigning to a different agent.

suggestions.msg: Clean unit test with a custom MockResult that correctly simulates SQLAlchemy result objects; covers get_ticket_replies ordering, get_ticket_activity ordering, and SLA breach detection without introducing any incorrect behavior or policy violations.

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: MagicMock() overrides the real async context-manager get_db with a plain lambda returning a MagicMock — this is a deviation from the real transaction lifecycle (commit on exit, rollback on exception). Acceptable here since the service layer is fully mocked, but fragile if a future test needs the real session.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider using an actual async context-manager mock (AsyncMock with __aenter__ returning self, __aexit__ returning None) for semantic accuracy, or add a comment documenting why a plain MagicMock suffices here.

issues.suggestion: Move the async delete call into handleDelete so the handler owns the complete action, not the JSX.

issues.message: initials() will return an empty string for names that are empty or contain only whitespace characters (split segments will be empty strings that are filtered to nothing by [0] access on empty strings).
issues.suggestion: Add a guard: if (!name?.trim()) return '?'; before the split.

issues.message: useEffect dependency array includes ticket and ticketId but not ticket.response_deadline — not strictly incorrect due to the ref guard, but incomplete for exhaustive-deps correctness.
issues.suggestion: Add ticket.response_deadline to the dependency array, or restructure so the condition is checked inside the effect body.

parsed.summary: Ticket detail page has a critical temporal dead zone ordering bug and an N+1 customer fetch; also contains dead code and incomplete form-field passing.

issues.message: useEffect cleanup returns a function that clears timerRef but timerRef is also set to null inside clearSearch — redundant but harmless.
issues.suggestion: Remove the useEffect entirely; the debounce timer is already cleared inside clearSearch and handleChange.

issues.message: handleDeleteTicket shows a window.confirm dialog instead of a styled UI dialog; this pattern inconsistently mixes browser-native UX with the design system.
issues.suggestion: Replace window.confirm with a dedicated confirmation dialog component, consistent with the edit/delete dialog pattern used elsewhere.

issues.message: handleViewTicket fires the SLA breach toast only when navigating to a ticket, even though breachedTicketIds is already shown in a batch toast on mount — redundant for the same user session.
issues.suggestion: Remove the toast from handleViewTicket since breached toasts already fire on page load, or scope it only to non-breached tickets visited from outside the list.

parsed.summary: Tickets list page has solid overall structure; minor issues include a redundant timer cleanup effect, a browser-native confirm dialog, and a potentially redundant per-row breach toast.

issues.message: useUsers is called inside the component body and then usersData is conditionally read inside an if block — this is technically fine because useUsers always runs, but it is fragile: adding any statement before the if that depends on usersData would break the rules-of-hooks ordering.
issues.suggestion: Move users extraction before the if block: `const users = (usersData?.data?.items ?? []) as ...; if (selectedIds.size === 0) return null;` — same pattern used in page.tsx.

parsed.summary: Bulk actions bar is straightforward and functional; one fragile hook ordering pattern that should be restated for safety.

issues.message: useEffect dependency array includes createdAt and slaLevel but neither is referenced inside the effect — changes to these props will not restart the interval, making the dependency list misleading.
issues.suggestion: Remove createdAt and slaLevel from the useEffect dependency array, or remove the empty deps comment if intentionally static.

parsed.summary: Functional kanban board with status/priority/assignee grouping; assignee labels show raw IDs rather than human-readable names.

issues.message: useEffect dependency array declares createdAt and slaLevel but neither is referenced in the effect body — the timer will not restart when these values change, making the deps misleading.
issues.suggestion: Remove createdAt and slaLevel from the dependency array, or add a comment explaining why they are absent.

issues.message: When breached is true, className is replaced with `${colorClass} animate-pulse border-red-500` and the incoming className prop is discarded — this silently drops the caller's className on breached tickets.
issues.suggestion: Merge className into the breached branch: `breached ? \`${colorClass} animate-pulse border-red-500 ${className ?? ""}\` : colorClass + (className ? \` \${className\}` : "")`

parsed.summary: SLA timer badge with color-coded elapsed ratio and overdue pulsing; relies on the less reliable ratio heuristic rather than comparing against the actual response_deadline.

issues.message: cn is imported from @/lib/utils but never used.
issues.suggestion: Remove the unused import.

issues.message: useCustomers is called with page=1, pageSize=20 to populate a dropdown selector, but only one customer is ever displayed at a time; no pagination controls exist for the dropdown, so a customer not on page 1 is unreachable.
issues.suggestion: Use useSearchCustomers with debouncing for the dropdown, or increase pageSize to a large value and rely on the Select UI for filtering.

issues.message: The channel, priority, and sla_level selects are hidden in edit mode, but their form values are never cleared; if the user toggles from edit back to create, stale values from the last create session may persist.
issues.suggestion: Reset channel, priority, and sla_level in the useEffect that resets the form when initialData changes.

issues.message: customer_id is not registered with react-hook-form — only a hidden input with a validator is used — so programmatic form inspection (e.g. formValues in onSubmit) may behave unexpectedly.
issues.suggestion: Register customer_id with register() and manage it via a controlled Select with onChange updating a hidden field, or use Controller.

parsed.summary: Full-featured ticket form dialog for create and edit modes with react-hook-form; customer dropdown may not scale beyond the first page of results.

issues.message: ApiEnvelope<T>.data is typed as PaginatedResponse<T>, which is wrong for non-paginated endpoints (slaBreaches, useReminders, useActivities single-item, etc.) — callers accessing .data.items will fail at runtime for those hooks.
issues.suggestion: Split ApiEnvelope into ApiEnvelope<T> with optional fields or a looser data type, or make data: T directly and adjust callers.

issues.message: useReminders calls apiClient.get without a type argument, and ApiEnvelope<PaginatedResponse<unknown>> is incorrectly applied to a non-paginated endpoint, so the return type is wrong.
issues.suggestion: Add the correct type argument to apiClient.get<...> and update ApiEnvelope usage for the reminders endpoint.

issues.message: Comments section header for Tasks is missing a leading // comment prefix and will be parsed as live code by some linters.
has_next is declared in PaginatedResponse but no hook uses it — pagination in callers relies on total and page_size for manual next/prev logic.
issues.suggestion: No fix needed; has_next is available for future use if callers add next-page buttons.

parsed.summary: Comprehensive React Query hooks for all API resources; incorrect ApiEnvelope typing for non-paginated endpoints is the most significant issue.

issues.message: mypy is listed in dev dependencies but no [tool.mypy] configuration exists in the file.
issues.suggestion: Add a [tool.mypy] table with at least ignores = ["attr-defined"] and strict = true (or a project-chosen baseline), and configure mypy.ini or pyproject.toml overrides so `mypy src/` runs with consistent settings across machines.

issues.message: Ruff formatter configuration is absent — only [tool.ruff.lint] is specified, so `ruff format` has no project-level settings (e.g. indent width, quote style) and will fall back to defaults.
issues.suggestion: Add [tool.ruff.format] with options matching the project's style (e.g. indent-width = 4, quote-style = "double") so formatting is deterministic and reproducible.

parsed.summary: Declarative, well-structured dependency manifest; needs formatter config and a mypy block to reach parity with its lint setup.

issues.message: HTTPException is imported but never raised in this file — all error paths delegate to the global AppException handler.
issues.suggestion: Remove the HTTPException import. If a future endpoint needs it, add it back then.

issues.message: assigned_to: ge=0 accepts 0 as valid, but the create_ticket handler treats 0 as a sentinel for 'unassigned', creating an inconsistency: a client can send assigned_to=0 but it will be silently interpreted as unassigned.
issues.suggestion: Remove the ge=0 constraint and let the TicketCreate schema omit assigned_to entirely when unassigned, matching the existing comment in list_tickets that documents 0 as 'unassigned'.

issues.message: bulk_update_tickets iterates over body.ticket_ids sequentially and calls update_ticket N times — N+1 query pattern (Rule 85). A single tenant with 500 tickets triggers 500 individual UPDATE calls.
issues.suggestion: Batch the update into one or two SQL statements: use `await session.execute(update(TicketModel).where(and_(TicketModel.id.in_(body.ticket_ids), TicketModel.tenant_id == ctx.tenant_id)).values(...))` for the common fields, then refresh the affected rows in a single query.

issues.message: bulk_update_tickets has no transaction scope across the loop — if the loop partially completes and an exception fires, some tickets are updated and some are not with no rollback.
issues.suggestion: Wrap the entire loop (or the batched query) in a try block, or restructure as a single batch UPDATE so all-or-nothing semantics are guaranteed by the router's commit lifecycle.

issues.message: Docstring says 'Tickets that do not exist or belong to a different tenant are skipped' but update_ticket raises NotFoundException for missing tickets, causing the loop to abort on the first missing ID rather than skip.
issues.suggestion: Catch NotFoundException inside the loop, log the skipped ID, and continue — matching the documented contract.

issues.message: check_sla_status endpoint creates two separate TicketService(session) instances (one for get_ticket, one inside SLAService constructor), and SLAService constructs a third TicketService at line 408.
issues.suggestion: Reuse a single TicketService instance across the endpoint's logic: pass ticket_svc = TicketService(session) into SLAService(session, ticket_service=ticket_svc) and remove the redundant construction at line 408.

parsed.summary: Follows the router pattern correctly; N+1 bulk update and missing skip-on-not-found are the critical issues, followed by the double TicketService construction in check_sla_status.

issues.message: ticket_service parameter has no type annotation and defaults to None — violates Rule 121/CLAUDE.md: 'Every service __init__ that takes a session must type it as AsyncSession with no default' and the same discipline should apply to injected dependencies.
issues.suggestion: Type the parameter as `ticket_service: TicketService | None = None` to make the optional contract explicit and catch type errors at static-analysis time.

issues.message: get_breach_tickets signature mixes two responsibilities — if tickets is provided it is filtered; if not, it is fetched from the injected ticket_service. The conditional at line 44 makes it unclear whether callers passing tickets intend to bypass the service query or are accidentally shadowing it.
issues.suggestion: Split into two methods: get_breach_tickets_from_list(tickets: list[Ticket]) for filtering a pre-fetched list, and get_breach_tickets(tenant_id: int) that always fetches via ticket_service. Remove the conditional.

issues.message: remaining.total_seconds() is called twice — once in the comparison and once to produce the warning threshold.
issues.suggestion: Compute it once: remaining_secs = remaining.total_seconds(); then use remaining_secs < warning_threshold * 3600 and remaining_secs for the hours calculation.

issues.message: The function-level type hint Literal["normal", "warning", "breached"] is returned at line 16 but get_breach_tickets at line 42 returns TicketModel objects (or list[Ticket]) — a docstring/return-type mismatch.
issues.suggestion: Ensure docstrings document actual return types accurately.

parsed.summary: Clean SLA logic with a well-named Literal return type, but the optional injected service with no type annotation is a pattern violation and the ambiguous get_breach_tickets signature needs splitting.

issues.message: _AGENT_POOL is a module-level constant (1, 2, 3) with no way to configure it per tenant or via environment — if the agent pool changes, the service must be edited and deployed.
issues.suggestion: Load from an environment variable or a config object: _AGENT_POOL = tuple(int(x) for x in os.environ.get("AGENT_POOL_IDS", "1,2,3").split(",")) so operators can change it without a code change.

issues.message: assigned_to.is_not(None) correctly filters non-null assignees but the intent comment in tickets.py line 154 treats 0 as 'unassigned' — if assigned_to=0 is ever stored, it would be counted as assigned here.
issues.suggestion: Clarify whether 0 is ever a valid assigned_to value in the database, and add a comment explaining the null-vs-0 distinction if they have different meanings.

issues.message: scalar() is used without checking whether the count query returned None — the fallback `or 0` is correct but the pattern is inconsistent with line 347 where the same fallback appears.
issues.suggestion: Add a comment or extract to a helper `_safe_count(result) -> int` to make the fallback intent explicit and reduce copy-paste risk.

issues.message: get_sla_breaches performs a full table scan filtering by tenant_id and resolved_at IS NULL — if the tickets table grows large, there is no index to support this query efficiently.
issues.suggestion: Verify an index exists on (tenant_id, resolved_at, response_deadline) or create one. Check via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on a realistic dataset.

issues.message: get_customer_tickets uses a LIKE pattern on ActivityModel.content (line 455) with string interpolation — while SQLAlchemy's .like() prevents injection, pattern-matching on a free-text content column prevents index usage.
issues.suggestion: If activity records are tied to a ticket via a ticket_id FK column, use that for the join instead of LIKE '%ticket#<id>%' to allow an index scan. If the current design is intentional, document the performance implication.

issues.message: get_ticket_activity silently returns an empty list when no matching activities are found — this is a valid state but the docstring does not clarify that an empty list is the expected return value rather than an error.
issues.suggestion: Add 'Returns an empty list if no activity records exist.' to the docstring for clarity.

parsed.summary: Well-structured service with clean SQL patterns and consistent flush-only transaction discipline; hardcoded agent pool and missing index on the SLA breach query are the primary concerns.

issues.message: Test 'test_assign_ticket' asserts `assigned_to is not None` on a freshly created ticket, but tickets are auto-assigned on creation (ticket_service.py:120-121). The assertion only confirms the pre-existing auto-assignment, not that assign_ticket can reassign an already-assigned ticket.
issues.suggestion: Split into two tests: (1) test that creation auto-assigns (assert assigned_to is not None), (2) test that assign_ticket can override an existing assignment by assigning to a different agent.

parsed.summary: Well-structured integration test suite with proper real DB usage and cross-service seeding; one test has an overly broad assertion that doesn't fully exercise the reassignment path.

Clean unit test with a custom MockResult that correctly simulates SQLAlchemy result objects; covers get_ticket_replies ordering, get_ticket_activity ordering, and SLA breach detection without introducing any incorrect behavior or policy violations.

issues.message: app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: MagicMock() overrides the real async context-manager get_db with a plain lambda returning a MagicMock — this is a deviation from the real transaction lifecycle (commit on exit, rollback on exception). Acceptable here since the service layer is fully mocked, but fragile if a future test needs the real session.
issues.suggestion: Consider using an actual async context-manager mock (AsyncMock with __aenter__ returning self, __aexit__ returning None) for semantic accuracy, or add a comment documenting why a plain MagicMock suffices here.

parsed.summary: Comprehensive router unit test covering all endpoints with proper FastAPI TestClient usage, monkeypatched services, and exception handler registration; minor fixture improvement opportunity on the get_db override.
